title: Emergency stop and jam clearing on cycling pusher machine
context: Automated production conveyors and pusher mechanisms are among the most common industrial sources of pinch and crushing injuries. When a workpiece jams, safety regulations mandate a strict emergency stop (E-STOP) protocol before any intervention. The operator must actuate the E-STOP to arrest the mechanism, extract the trapped object from the danger zone, and only then perform an orderly RESET and START sequence. Clearing a jam while the pusher is cycling creates an immediate catastrophic hazard and results in a safety fault.
instruction: Press the red E-STOP so the pusher stops, take the stuck orange block out of the lane, then press RESET and START: never reach into the lane while the pusher is moving.
setup: All positions are cm from the midpoint between arm bases (x forward, y left); table top is z = 0. Lane: 30.0 x 15.0 x 2.0 cm walled channel at (34.0, +10.0 cm) with 1.0 cm thick, 2.0 cm tall perimeter walls enclosing a designated danger zone (x in [19.0, 49.0 cm], y in [2.5, 17.5 cm], z up to 12.0 cm). Pusher: 3.0 x 12.0 x 2.5 cm non-colliding bar sweeping along x over 9.0 cm with 4.0 s period. Stuck block: 4.0 cm orange cube (0.045 kg) at (40.0, +10.0 cm). Button console: rigid base plate at y = -20.0 cm with three 0.8 cm travel, 100 N/m spring pushbuttons in a row along x: red 6.0 cm E-STOP cap at (28.0, -20.0 cm), white 4.0 cm RESET cap at (34.0, -20.0 cm), and green 4.0 cm START cap at (40.0, -20.0 cm). Indicator lamps (2.5 cm discs): STOP (red) at (28.0, -15.5 cm), FAULT (amber) at (34.0, -15.5 cm), and RUN (green) at (40.0, -15.5 cm). Green tray: 13.0 x 13.0 x 2.0 cm receptacle at (30.0, +30.0 cm).
scoring: Score: 0.25 when E-STOP is pressed and pusher stops safely without fault (latched ever_stopped); 0.50 when stuck block is extracted from lane into green tray (or RESET pressed after E-STOP without fault); 0.75 when RESET then START are pressed in order with block out of lane (pusher restarts, RUN lamp lit); 1.00 when both arms are clear of danger zone and end state is held for 2.0 s (40 steps at 20 Hz). Zero-gates: any arm TCP entering lane danger zone while pusher is moving triggers an immediate FAULT (score 0.0); pressing START while block is still in lane triggers FAULT (score 0.50).
reset_notes: Verify pusher is cycling along lane and RUN lamp is lit. Confirm orange block is placed at (40.0, +10.0 cm) in lane. Confirm E-STOP, RESET, and START buttons are in uncompressed resting positions. Confirm green tray is empty and STOP/FAULT lamps are dark.
fidelity: Pusher is a code-driven non-colliding visual bar sweeping along X (period 4.0 s, 90 mm stroke); the danger zone is enforced as a strict geometric boundary rule rather than rigid body contact. Buttons are physical prismatic sliders with 100 N/m spring return, 8 mm travel to stop, and viscous damping. Stuck block is a physical rigid body. Lamps are visual markers updated via write_pose. Real-world basis: industrial machine safeguarding, OSHA/ISO 13850 E-STOP recovery.
